source_document.body:
Walmart is adding 300 Zipline drone delivery sites under a new multi-year agreement, expanding a service that brings items to customers’ homes in as little as 30 minutes. The deal leaves room for more sites beyond that commitment.
What’s Related
Zipline also announced $1.5 billion in funding to expand its U.S. manufacturing facilities, hire more staff and build a nationwide drone delivery network. The round values the company at $21.5 billion after the investment.
Walmart has worked with Zipline on drone deliveries since 2021. The retailer said its drone delivery program has completed more than 2 million deliveries, including deliveries from Zipline.
From store to home
The expansion builds on Walmart’s stores as starting points for home deliveries. The retailer said 90% of Americans live within 10 miles of a Walmart.
“We see customers try drone delivery for the novelty and then continue to come back to it for the convenience when they need something in minutes,” said Greg Cathey, Walmart’s senior vice president of eCommerce Fulfillment Transformation. “Walmart’s stores put us close to the communities we serve. With Zipline, we can build on that proximity and bring this fast delivery option to even more customers across the country.”
RELATED STORIES: Walmart Expands Drone Delivery to 150 More U.S. Locations | Massachusetts Wants to Hit Pause on Amazon’s Drone Delivery Plans
Customers with eligible addresses can select drone delivery in the Walmart app or on Walmart.com. Customers with eligible addresses can also order through the Zipline app. Tens of thousands of items are eligible.
Deliveries go to a front yard, backyard, or driveway. The aircraft stays roughly 330 feet above the ground while a tether lowers a pod carrying the order.
Drone delivery sits alongside Walmart’s other options, including one-hour-or-less Express delivery and scheduled delivery.
Betting on Speed
Zipline’s pitch to customers and investors is speed. The company said its median order in October arrived 19 minutes after checkout, compared with 30-plus minutes for traditional delivery. Bakery orders were even faster, arriving in a median of 10 minutes.
Zipline said it has made more than 1 million deliveries in Dallas-Fort Worth alone this year. Uber is aiming even higher, targeting 1 million deliveries a day with Zipline by 2029.
The new funding will help Zipline expand its U.S. manufacturing facilities and hire more people, though the company didn’t say how much will go to each or how many jobs it plans to add. Paradigm, WCM Investment Management, and Layer Global led the round, with Uber, Fidelity, and Salesforce Ventures among the other investors.
“Zipline has already brought the future of delivery to the communities it serves. Now, the opportunity is to reach millions more,” said Anton Levy, founder and managing partner of Layer Global.
Other Walmart News
$6 Billion Symbotic Expansion : Walmart committed approximately $6 billion to expand its Symbotic agreement, including additional automation at 25 U.S. regional distribution centers .
Warehouse Automation Challenges : Walmart plans to replace shipping boxes that do not fit its automated systems as its warehouse upgrades face packaging problems, robot repairs and higher electricity costs, according to The Wall Street Journal.
Stockton, California, Fulfillment Center Opens : Walmart opened an automated fulfillment center spanning more than 900,000 square feet to handle West Coast online orders. The facility is expected to create more than 1,000 jobs .
ShipStation Adds Walmart Shipping Rates : ShipStation launched Ship with Walmart, giving U.S. Marketplace sellers access to Walmart-negotiated shipping rates and up to $100 in protection for eligible lost-item claims.
$1.3 Billion Georgia Fulfillment Center Planned : Walmart plans a 1.5 million-square-foot automated fulfillment center in Carnesville, Georgia, expected to create 1,000 jobs. Construction is scheduled to begin in late 2026.
